name: English Longbow Laws, Edward I's Military Revolution
summary: Henry III's Assize of Arms (1252) and Edward III's later archery statutes require English and Welsh free men to practice archery regularly. The resulting pool of trained longbowmen, capable of shooting 10-12 aimed arrows per minute with 100-180 lb draw weight, creates a tactical asset unavailable to any other European kingdom. Welsh longbowmen from the Marches provide the technical expertise; English practice laws spread the skill.

_quarry.structural_significance: The English longbow investment demonstrates how systematic training policy can create decisive military advantage; the longbow requires 10+ years of practice (evidenced by archers' skeletal deformities from sustained training), it cannot be improvised; this training system distinguishes English tactics from continental armies that attempt to substitute mercenary crossbowmen; Crécy, Poitiers, and Agincourt are all consequences of this long-term investment
